title: IELTS Speaking — A Useful Skill (Full Mock)

parts.title: Part 1 — Introduction and interview
parts.instructions: Before the recorded interview begins, the examiner will check your identity and confirm your identification documents. This is not scored. The scored Part 1 then begins with general questions about yourself and a few familiar topics. Answer naturally and try to extend each answer with a reason or example. This part lasts 4–5 minutes.

questions.question: Let's talk about hobbies. Do you have any hobbies?
How did you first become interested in this hobby?
Do you think it's important for people to have hobbies?
Now let's talk about weekends. What do you usually do at the weekend?
Do you prefer spending weekends alone or with other people?
Has the way you spend your weekends changed since you were younger?
Let's move on to your neighbourhood. Do you know your neighbours well?
What do you like about the area where you live?
Would you like to live somewhere else in the future? Why or why not?

parts.title: Part 2 — Individual long turn
parts.instructions: You will be given a topic card. You have one minute to prepare and may make notes. Then speak for one to two minutes. Try to keep talking until the examiner stops you.
parts.cue_card_topic: Describe a useful skill you have learned.
cue_card_bullets: how and where you learned it
how long it took you to learn
and explain why this skill has been useful to you

questions.question: Is there another skill you would like to learn in the future?

parts.title: Part 3 — Two-way discussion
parts.instructions: The examiner will ask further questions connected to the Part 2 topic. These are more abstract and require you to explain, compare, and speculate. Try to give extended, well-reasoned answers. This part lasts 4–5 minutes.

questions.question: What skills do you think are most important for young people to learn today?
Do you think schools teach students the practical skills they need for life? Why or why not?
Some people say practical skills are more valuable than academic qualifications. Do you agree?
How has technology changed the way people learn new skills?
Do you think it's necessary for adults to keep learning new skills throughout their lives?
How might the skills people need for work change over the next few decades?
